meta.title: Redistribution
meta.question: Should the state reduce the gap between rich and poor?
meta.measure: Average position on redistribution, from 0 (for redistribution from rich to poor) to 10 (against)
meta.anchor: Pooled from every question on reducing income differences, with every answer placed on 0 to 10 and the trend read on the scale of an average question.

items.wording: Incomes should be made more equal (1) vs we need larger income differences as incentives for individual effort (10)
items.notes: European Values Study 1990, 1999, 2008, 2017 (4 surveys). In EVS 2008 it barely correlates with the battery's other economic items (not reversed: it relates to education as in the other waves).

items.wording: Should it be the government's responsibility to reduce income differences?
items.notes: Consolidation of Democracy in CEE, 1991 and 2000.

items.wording: Should there be large, some or no differences in income?
items.notes: Consolidation of Democracy in CEE, 1991 and 2000.

items.wording: Should differences in income be larger, as now, or smaller?
The government should reduce differences in income (agree-disagree)
items.notes: Polish General Social Survey 1992-2010; code 3, mislabelled, is the midpoint.

items.wording: Large income differences are necessary for Poland's prosperity (agree-disagree)
items.notes: POLPAN 1988, 1993, 1998, 2003, 2013, 2018 (6; not 2008). Label 'income differences are necessary' to 1998, '...necessary to assure prosperity' from 2003, same slot (the ISSP item). 1988 and 1993 subsamples as above; 2013 asked of 79%. It correlates -0.14 to -0.25 with the egalitarian items in 1988-2003 but only -0.05 (2013) and -0.02 (2018), when the battery is dominated by agreement: exclude POLPAN 2013 and 2018 (exclusions.csv).

items.wording: Income differences in Poland are too large (agree-disagree)
items.notes: POLPAN 1988, 1993, 1998, 2003 (4; 1988 and 1993 subsamples as POLPAN_STATE_INCDIFF). A judgement on inequality rather than on state action, from the same egalitarian battery.

items.wording: Should there be a legal limit on the highest monthly income? (yes / no)
items.notes: POLPAN 1988 and 1993 (all respondents). From 1998 an agree-disagree statement: POLPAN_INCOME_CAP.

items.wording: The state should reduce differences in incomes (agree-disagree)
items.notes: POLPAN 1988-2018, 7 waves. Asked of one questionnaire version in 1988 (1,959 of 5,817) and of about half in 1993 (1,162 of 2,259), of all from 1998. English label 'decrease inequality' to 1998, 'reduce differences in incomes' from 2003, same battery slot. 2013 repeats it in a short module for part of the sample (UZP1B); the regex leaves that copy out.

items.wording: The earnings of the highest paid should be capped vs should not be capped
items.notes: CBOS's two-statement self-placement cards (the PGSW battery's format).

items.wording: Incomes should be made more equal (1) vs we need larger income differences as incentives (10)
items.notes: World Values Survey 1989, 1997, 2005, 2012 (4). In 1989 the four economic 1-10 items hardly correlate with one another.

items.wording: Should it be the government's responsibility to reduce income differences between the rich and the poor?
It should be the government's duty to reduce differences between the well paid and the badly paid (agree-disagree)
There should be an upper limit on incomes that no one could exceed (agree-disagree)
For a just society, how important is eliminating big inequalities in income between citizens? (very important ... not at all important)
items.notes: EVS 1999 (1-5). Very consensual (77% very or quite important).

items.wording: There should be no limit on incomes vs a limit is necessary
items.notes: Consolidation of Democracy in CEE, 1991 and 2000 (85% 'no limit' in 1991, 22% in 2000). 'Can't choose' (2000 only, 6%) is ISSP's don't know and is left out.

items.wording: Important: that there are no big income differences (very ... not important)
items.notes: CDCEE 2000 only (battery not asked in Poland in 1991).

items.wording: Wide income differences are not good for society (agree-disagree)
Income differences in Poland are too wide (agree-disagree)
items.notes: Candidate Countries Eurobarometer 2002.1 (March 2002, ZA4153); codes run from 1 strongly disagree to 5 strongly agree.

items.wording: The government should take measures to reduce differences in income levels (agree-disagree)
Large differences in people's incomes are acceptable to properly reward differences in talents and efforts (agree-disagree)
For a fair society, differences in people's standard of living should be small (agree-disagree)
Income and wealth should be redistributed towards ordinary people (agree-disagree)
The Polish government should ensure that the country's wealth is fairly distributed among all citizens (agree-disagree)
Income differences between people in Poland are far too large (agree-disagree)
Income inequalities are necessary for economic development (agree-disagree)
items.notes: Eurobarometer 72.1 (2009). Correlates weakly (-0.05 to -0.11) but with the right sign with the module's egalitarian items.

items.wording: The government should take action to reduce differences in income levels (agree-disagree)
Redistribution of wealth from the rich to the poor: fully in favour (0) ... fully opposed (10)
items.notes: EES 2014; codes 1-11 stand for 0-10. Its eight 0-10 questions share one variable label, so the value labels pick the question. 'Do not know' (-9) is not caught by the DK pattern and is simply left out.

items.wording: Eliminating big income inequalities, as above, 1-4
Redistribution of wealth from the rich to the poor: fully favour (0) ... fully oppose (10)
Large income differences are needed to reward differences in ability and effort (agree-disagree)
In a just society, differences in income should be small (agree-disagree)
The government should take measures to reduce differences in income levels (agree-disagree)
items.notes: SWPS COVID tracker wave 14 (July 2021), online; the ESS gincdif wording.

items.wording: In a just society, differences in income should be small (agree-disagree)
The government should take measures to reduce differences in income levels (agree-disagree)
items.notes: ESS round 10 (2021-22): self-completion by web and paper in Poland, where every other round was face to face, so a question of its own.
